message.content: The total number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—roughly on the order of **\(10^{43}\)**. This estimate comes from counting all possible ways the pieces can be arranged on the board while respecting the rules of movement and capture, including considerations such as castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, and pawn promotion choices. In contrast, the number of possible complete games (i.e., sequences of moves from start to finish) is even larger, often cited as about \(10^{120}\).
